title: Love's Assassin: Self-justification in Marriage
coreMove: Translate one permanent indictment back into the specific situation before the argument becomes a trial of the other person's character.
sourcePressure: The marriage chapter applies self-justification to intimate conflict: people explain their own bad behavior by circumstance and their partner's by character, then store grievance as proof.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Turning the chapter into generic relationship advice, apology scripts, or equal-blame smoothing instead of attribution asymmetry and stored grievance.

sourceAnchors.name: happy versus unhappy partner framing
sourceAnchors.detail: the source supports the contrast that more stable couples grant situational grace, while unhappy couples treat good acts as flukes and bad acts as character proof
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: A stable couple still sees the bad moment; the difference is that they have not turned every bad moment into a biography.

sourceAnchors.name: attribution split
sourceAnchors.detail: the source supports the pattern of excusing one's own behavior through circumstance while reading a partner's behavior as character
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The assassin is small at first: my sharpness was stress, your sharpness was who you really are.

hook: Do not start with a generic kitchen fight.
counterintuition: Do not say both sides are equally wrong in every conflict.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person direct address, retrospective realization, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'

exampleSpecs.domain: a breakfast argument over a forgotten allergy-safe school snack
exampleSpecs.audience: parents whose logistical stress turns into character accusations
exampleSpecs.stakes: a preventable miss becomes evidence that one partner does not care
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Emily stops before saying "you never think" and names the exact calendar handoff that failed
exampleSpecs.firstImage: an unopened sunflower-butter snack bar beside a school permission slip

exampleSpecs.domain: a daycare pickup conflict after a delayed train
exampleSpecs.audience: couples where one partner's lateness becomes a character trial
exampleSpecs.stakes: pickup stress becomes another entry in a permanent unreliability file
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Vincent repeats the accusation in situational terms, train delay plus no backup call, before defending himself
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a paper daycare late-fee slip curled in a coat pocket

exampleSpecs.domain: a renovation budget meeting between spouses after a surprise plumbing bill
exampleSpecs.audience: partners whose money arguments turn one error into identity proof
exampleSpecs.stakes: a shared repair project becomes a file of selfishness and control
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Maja writes "bad estimate" and "secret spending" in separate columns before choosing which claim the evidence can support
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a cracked ceramic tile balanced on top of a contractor invoice

exampleSpecs.domain: a holiday visit where one spouse remembers every slight from the other's family
exampleSpecs.audience: readers carrying a grievance archive into recurring family events
exampleSpecs.stakes: the visit will be fought before anyone arrives if old memory becomes current proof
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You watch Jack sort last year's actual incidents from the character verdict he has attached to them before the guest room is made
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a folded guest towel resting on an unopened train timetable

exampleSpecs.domain: new parents arguing over night feeds after three weeks without sleep
exampleSpecs.audience: couples under strain who mistake exhaustion for character evidence
exampleSpecs.stakes: one missed bottle becomes proof of selfishness while both partners are depleted
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: It takes Kasia three weeks to see that her partner's worst moment happened after two night shifts, then she changes the repair request
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a sterilized bottle standing in a saucepan of cooling water

exampleSpecs.domain: a retirement-planning disagreement after one spouse hides anxiety about savings
exampleSpecs.audience: long-term partners who turn fear into accusation
exampleSpecs.stakes: a practical money conversation becomes a verdict on courage and trust
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Aman places the pension statement beside the angry text and identifies the fear before either partner argues character
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a pension statement folded into thirds beside reading glasses

skillTargets: distinguish situational explanation from character indictment
choose repair language that preserves accountability without prosecution
analyze how stored grievance changes the purpose of arguing

tryThisNowSpec: Take one complaint about someone close to you and rewrite it from "they are" into "in that moment, under these conditions, they did..." without excusing the harm.
